heroHeadline: IDF Halts Artillery Under US Pressure but Two Children Still Killed; Top IDF Officer Calls Settler Violence 'Jewish Terror,' Warns of Palestinian Uprising
heroSubtitle: Israel suspended most artillery fire into Gaza on May 1, 2026, following intense U.S. diplomatic pressure — but the Palestinian Health Ministry confirmed at least two Palestinian children were killed by Israeli fire on the same day marking six months since the October 2025 ceasefire. IDF Central Command Chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth issued an extraordinary public warning calling escalating settler attacks 'Jewish terror' and cautioning that 59 West Bank communities have been fully depopulated in 2026, placing the territory on the edge of a new Palestinian uprising. Erez crossing was reopened for the first time in months under US pressure. The Global Sumud Flotilla aftermath continues: 168 detained activists were transferred to Crete by Greek authorities, while 47 vessels resumed their voyage toward Gaza.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Euronews, Haaretz, Times of Israel, Yesh Din, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
